 Women And Family Ministry Readies 25 Counsellors To Support Flood Victims
 By BusinessToday 
 November 20, 2026 
 Share 
 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin 
 The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has deployed 25 counsellors to provide psychosocial support, counselling and crisis intervention to flood victims at temporary relief centres (PPS) in Selangor.
 Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the counsellors, comprising officers from the Social Welfare Department (JKM) and the Malaysian Board of Counsellors, would prioritise vulnerable groups, particularly women, the elderly and children, including students preparing for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examinations. 
 She said more than 1,000 people had been displaced by floods in Selangor, with Kuala Selangor among the worst-affected areas, experiencing flooding for the past 16 days.
 The counsellors would adopt age-specific approaches to address evacuees’ concerns and help them prepare for their return home once floodwaters receded, she said after visiting the SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela relief centre in Jeram today.
 The centre, which opened on Nov 5, was sheltering 394 evacuees from 102 families as of this morning, following prolonged flooding in several surrounding areas, including Kampung Bukit Kuching and Kampung Bukit Hijau.
 Nancy said 35 JKM personnel were stationed at relief centres around Kuala Selangor, supported by the department’s 1,100 personnel in Selangor.
 She added that the ministry was also looking to mobilise more volunteers to assist affected communities and prepare for potential flooding in other parts of the country.
 Meanwhile, flood assistance for victims registered with JKM was proceeding smoothly, including the distribution of additional special cash aid at the relief centre.
 On Nov 9, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced a one-off payment of RM2,500 for each eligible head of household affected by floods in Selangor, with the state government providing a further RM500.
 A flood victim, Rahman Asroo, 63, from Kampung Bukit Hijau, said the assistance would help ease his family’s financial burden after their home and restaurant were inundated, leaving them without an income source.
